summary: line_clip_lerp() now computes `float z = mix(pa.z * ia, pb.z * ib, t) * w;` -- one factor of 1/w inside the mix and one w outside. pa.z * ia is the endpoint's window-space depth, the mix is taken at the screen fraction tl the caller passes, and multiplying by w returns it to clip space, so z/w at the cut point is mix(za/wa, zb/wb, t), which is what the rasteriser interpolates across the parallelogram the cut vertex replaces. The comment above it was rewritten from the correct rule and names the old expression as the defect.
scenario: Pass 1's scenario -- a wide line in perspective with w_a = 1, w_b = 4 and endpoint NDC depths 0.2 and 0.8, whose cut vertices read 0.246/0.320/0.457 where the truth is 0.350/0.500/0.650 -- can no longer occur. line_cap_phase.py --depth, run on this host, transliterates the shipped expression and the pre-remediation one over 75 cases including that exact pair: shipped worst |error| 1.11e-16, mutant worst |error| 0.583. The mutant is inside the check and the check reports FAIL about itself if the old expression does not trip it, so the green is not a check that discriminates nothing; I read depth_check() to confirm the second leg is real rather than only reading its PASS.
evidence: hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/glsl/geom.c:317-357 (line_clip_lerp and its rewritten comment), :483-484 (call site at the screen fraction tl); docs/testing/line_cap_phase.py:551-608 (depth_check, both expressions and the mutant leg); `python3 line_cap_phase.py --depth` run at tip 1d4e5aa14b.

summary: geom.c:719 tells the reader the cap clip 'is inert below w = 24, where E/2 - w/2 is under a pixel', and emit_line_vertex()'s comment adds that the unclipped four-corner case emits what it emitted before 'bit for bit'. Both hold for the pixels the offline model scores and not for the geometry the device is handed. E/2 - w/2 being under a pixel does not stop the clip biting: the bounds are floor(m_min - w/2) and ceil(m_max + w/2) + 1, arbitrary reals rounded to integers, so a tenth-of-a-pixel overhang crosses one whenever a corner lands near it. Counting edges whose shader_poly() returns more than four vertices at the shipped 1/256 tie, every capture from w = 0.625 up is clipped on 3 to 20 of its 57 edges before w reaches 24 (w=1: 9 edges, deepest sliver 0.020 px; w=4: 17, 0.114; w=8: 18, 0.232; w=13: 11, 0.301; w=16: 20, 0.468; w=24: 25, 0.704). Below w = 24 the sliver is under half a pixel so no pixel centre changes side in float64, which is why --rivals, --controls and --shader all report the change as inert there. The device computes the cut fraction f = da/(da - db) in float32 from a da that is a sliver depth, snaps every emitted vertex to 1/256 of a pixel, and then decides centre membership.
scenario: Already measured, by the arms job on this PR. VERDICT: FAIL, a_ref 2e1c5790aa (master) against b_ref 9fdc6b5d70 (this branch), one run each, suite Line_width: 10 captures worse, 8 of them at w = 4, 6, 7, 9, 10, 12, 13 and 14 (+1, +2, +2, +1, +2, +5, +9, +1), inside the range the comment says the change cannot touch. Five more below w = 24 moved the other way (w = 1, 8, 11, 15, 16 at -1, -1, -1, -5, -1), and Line_0064.0 through .7 and Line_FFFFFFFF each moved 1,402 -> 1,401 -- the same value, the same direction, nine captures at once, which is not the shape of a single-run flake. Thirteen scored captures below w = 24 moved where all three of this lane's instruments say not one pixel can change; I reproduced that blindness here by rasterising the clipped and unclipped polygons capture by capture at both tie biases, where the first row that moves at all is Line_0024.0 (935 -> 544 at 1/256, 414 -> 21 at 1e-9, nothing below 24 in either). The prediction's machine-read leg is expect_counts {"worse": 0} and it failed; the PR carries regressed; nothing on the PR has answered it. The consequence beyond the eight captures is the comment: it tells the next reader this change cannot reach narrow lines, so a narrow-line regression will not be traced here.
remediation: 1. Stop the clip biting where it cannot matter: a cut shallower than the device's own vertex quantum can only move pixels by re-quantising an edge that was previously exact, so skipping cap_clip() on a plane the polygon violates by less than one quantum (lineTieBias is already in the push constant) leaves the w >= 24 result untouched -- the deepest sliver there is 0.70 px and up -- and restores the bit-for-bit claim below it. Derive the threshold and state it; do not pick 24. 2. Make an instrument see it: shader_poly() rasterises in double precision and never snaps a vertex to the 1/256 grid, so it is blind to exactly the class of change the arm measured; quantising each emitted vertex to lineTieBias before the coverage test, and reporting the per-capture bite count, would have caught this offline. --depth is the model for the shape. 3. Re-register and let the arms job re-judge: arms.sh clears regressed from the verdicts, not by hand, and a second pair also settles how much of the plus-or-minus one pixel is run-to-run, since noise 0 in that verdict is one run per arm with nothing to estimate from rather than a measured zero. Correct both comments either way; if the narrow-line movement is an acceptable price for the wide end, that is a regression-accepted argument for the owner on #13, not a comment saying it did not happen.
evidence: hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/glsl/geom.c:714-721 (the inertness claim), :425-434 (the bit-for-bit claim), :531-566 (cap_clip and its f = da/(da-db)), :760-787 (the two cap_clip calls and the bounds); docs/testing/line_cap_phase.py:267-327 (shader_poly and shader_mask, both float64, no vertex quantisation); the [job.arms] VERDICT: FAIL comment on PR #141 dated 2026-09-19T16:50:19Z; bite counts from len(shader_poly(e, w, 1/256)) > 4 over lp.EDGES for every non-void capture, and the clipped-vs-unclipped coverage comparison at tie 1/256 and 1e-9, both run at tip 1d4e5aa14b.

summary: controls() counts both m_min - w/2 and m_max + w/2 into ties_int and prints the total as 'the population that separates tie=ceil from tie=floor1'. Only the high boundary can: edge_mask() computes plo with np.floor(...) for every tie value and the tie switch reaches phi alone, so a low boundary landing on an integer is floored identically by both rules.
scenario: A reader of --controls, and of the PR comment that quotes it, is told 1,104 of 5,472 boundaries separate the shipped outward rounding from floor + 1. Split over the same captures the 1,104 is 617 low-side and 487 high-side, so the figure is 2.3x the population it names. The conclusion survives -- 487 is not zero, so the goldens do select the outward rounding, which is the question pass 1's M3 asked -- which is why this is LOW and does not reopen M3.
remediation: Count m_max + w/2 alone for the integer population, or print both halves with the low side labelled as not separating anything.
